articles.title: Mais que compras: supermercado é local para descobrir, comer, resolver e ficar | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre carnes especiais, vinhos, produtos importados, gastronomia, flores e serviços, o Ítalo Barigui transforma uma ida ao supermercado em uma experiência.
articles.summary: Entre carnes especiais, vinhos, produtos importados, gastronomia, flores e serviços, o Ítalo Barigui transforma uma ida ao supermercado em uma experiência.
articles.body:
Tem dias em que a gente entra no supermercado sabendo exatamente o que precisa. Em outros, basta uma volta pelos corredores para descobrir alguma coisa que muda o jantar, o churrasco do fim de semana ou até o presente que faltava para alguém.

Pode ser uma carne diferente para impressionar os amigos, um vinho escolhido para acompanhar a refeição, flores para levar para casa ou simplesmente um café moído na hora. É nessa combinação de necessidade e descoberta que o supermercado ganha uma função diferente na rotina.

No Supermercado Conceito Ítalo Barigui , inaugurado em Curitiba, a proposta é justamente reunir essas possibilidades em um mesmo endereço , aproximando compras, gastronomia, serviços e momentos de convivência.

Imagine que você decidiu receber amigos em casa. No mesmo passeio, pode escolher um corte especial no açougue, procurar uma carne exótica, encomendar uma peça para maturação Dry Aged, passar pela fiambreria para escolher queijos e frios fatiados na hora e seguir até a adega para encontrar um vinho que combine com o cardápio.

Se a ideia for preparar uma pizza, o Ítalo Barigui pode preparar uma deliciosa sob sua escolha e massa de fermentação longa para levar para casa. E, para quem prefere comer no próprio local, o restaurante oferece buffet durante o dia e à noite. Viva essa experiência .

A lógica é menos a de um supermercado que simplesmente reúne produtos e mais a de um espaço em que uma compra pode inspirar o que vem depois.

Um passeio pelos corredores pode render descobertas

Parte dessa experiência está na curadoria. Entre os produtos encontrados no Ítalo Barigui estão itens importados e produtos sofisticados, além de ingredientes de diferentes partes do mundo escolhidos para quem gosta de experimentar sabores novos.

A seleção gastronômica também reúne marcas especializadas. Há cafés especiais da Distinto , Lucca e Moka Club , com moagem na hora, culinária japonesa do Taisho , doces da Délices de Sucre , massas artesanais da L'Artigiana e Rosmarino , temperos da Cipria e pescados da Trapiche .

São produtos que podem tanto entrar na lista de compras quanto despertar uma ideia para o almoço, o jantar ou aquela mesa preparada para receber convidados.

E o horário ajuda: o Ítalo Barigui funciona até 23h , permitindo que uma compra de última hora também faça parte da rotina. Aos domingos e feriados, a unidade funciona até as 22h. Confira como os clientes têm falado do Ítalo Barigui.

A grande oferta de produtos e variedade de tipos de alimentos do Ítalo Barigui é um convite para ampliar o cardápio em casa. — Foto: Divulgação/Nenad Radovanovic.

Para quem procura outras formas de se alimentar

A experiência também passa pela área de saudabilidade. O supermercado reúne produtos naturais, funcionais e suplementos, além de uma padaria totalmente dedicada à produção de alimentos sem glúten , com estrutura e equipamentos independentes.

Ali, pães, bolos e outros produtos são preparados dentro de uma operação pensada especificamente para esse tipo de produção, com cuidados para evitar a contaminação cruzada.

É uma alternativa para quem busca produtos sem glúten por necessidade, preferência ou simplesmente quer experimentar outras possibilidades de alimentação.

O Ítalo Barigui também foi pensado para que o consumidor possa permanecer no espaço. A estrutura reúne supermercado, restaurante e varanda no segundo andar, além de oferecer estacionamento, carregamento para veículos elétricos, ambiente pet friendly, além de um atendimento com proximidade.

Quem chega de carro pode resolver as compras enquanto recarrega o veículo. Quem está acompanhado do pet, encontra um espaço preparado para recebê-lo. Quem foi apenas almoçar pode aproveitar a visita para comprar os ingredientes que faltam em casa.

Há ainda o Concierge Ítalo , profissional que acompanha o cliente durante as compras, e o atendimento especializado na adega para quem precisa de ajuda na escolha de vinhos e harmonizações.

São serviços que fazem diferença justamente porque não aparecem necessariamente na lista de compras.

O conceito de "novo jeito de viver o supermercado" , adotado pelo Grupo Ítalo, aparece justamente nessa possibilidade de combinar diferentes momentos em uma mesma visita. Click e conheça .

Ítalo Barigui está localizado na Rua Pedro Viriato Parigot de Souza, 565.

Ítalo Barigui. Perto de casa, longe do comum.

articles.title: Ex-marido condenado a pagar gastos de casamento não pagava contas | G1
articles.standfirst: Casamento durou 29 dias, diante de comportamento abusivo do homem, reconhecido pelo juiz. Ele determinou o pagamento de mais de R$ 18 mil à ex-mulher, mas o ex-companheiro vai recorrer da decisão.
articles.summary: Casamento durou 29 dias, diante de comportamento abusivo do homem. Justiça determinou o pagamento de mais de R$ 18 mil à ex-mulher, mas o ex-companheiro vai recorrer.
articles.body:
O ex-marido que foi condenado pela Justiça a pagar gastos com festa de casamento e lua de mel depois da união ter chegado ao fim em apenas 29 dias não arcava com as contas durante relacionamento. Essa informação foi trazida por testemunhas durante o processo judicial. O homem foi condenado a pagar mais de R$ 18 mil à ex-mulher.

Em nota enviada ao g1 , a defesa do ex-marido disse que não vai comentar o caso, por ser assunto ligado à vida privada e familiar, mas que vai recorrer da decisão ( leia a íntegra da nota ao final da reportagem ).

O caso aconteceu em 2022, em Anápolis , na região central de Goiás. O casamento durou de maio a junho daquele ano. Na época, a mulher tinha 41 anos e o homem, 36. No ano seguinte, ela moveu uma ação de Indenização por perdas e danos contra ele, pedindo ressarcimento de R$ 13.658,60, referente à metade das despesas que ela teve com o casório, e pagamento de R$ 10 mil por danos morais. A justiça reconheceu ambos, mas reduziu o segundo à metade, para R$ 5 mil.

No processo, uma testemunha afirmou que as despesas da festa foram pagas exclusivamente pela então noiva. O noivo arcou apenas com a compra das bebidas, mesmo assim com a ajuda de amigos, por meio de doações.

Em depoimento, uma funcionária doméstica da mulher disse que "99% dos gastos" eram pagos por ela e que o homem se recusava a arcar com as despesas cotidianas, prometendo repassar o dinheiro depois.

Além disso, uma das madrinhas do casamento relatou que, nos encontros sociais aos quais o casal ia, era a mulher quem pagava as contas.

Segundo o advogado da ex-mulher, Gabriel Divino Silva Elias, o relacionamento terminou a pedido dela, que precisou, inclusive, solicitar à Justiça uma medida protetiva contra o ex, que foi renovada após essa sentença da ação por perdas e danos.

"Além das ameaças que vinha sofrendo, ela se deu conta que tinha sido vítima de estelionato amoroso, o que foi reconhecido na sentença", relatou o advogado.

Na decisão, proferida no último dia 9 de setembro, o juiz Thiago Inácio de Oliveira afirmou que as provas demonstraram um "padrão de comportamento abusivo" por parte do ex-marido.

"(O homem) se utilizou da confiança inerente à relação afetiva para obter vantagem patrimonial indevida, impondo à requerente uma sobrecarga financeira significativa e gerando-lhe frustração e abalo emocional", disse o magistrado.

Juiz considerou que a relação do homem no casamento que durou 29 dias foi abusiva e determinou pagamento de indenização — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

No processo, o ex-marido alegou que a ação movida pela ex-esposa era motivada por um mero aborrecimento com o fim do relacionamento. O juiz, no entanto, não aceitou o argumento, dizendo que a conduta do homem, ao criar expectativa de cooperação financeira, que era frustrada posteriormente de forma repetida, atingiu os direitos de "personalidade, dignidade e tranquilidade psíquica" da mulher.

"Diante desse cenário, o que se denota é a materialização do enriquecimento sem causa do requerido, (...), uma vez que se beneficiou economicamente do patrimônio da requerente sem a devida contraprestação", disse.

No processo, a mulher afirmou ter sido vítima de estelionato sentimental.

🔍 Estelionato sentimental é, segundo o Instituto Brasileiro de Direito de Família (IBDFAM), a situação em que uma das pessoas está envolvida no relacionamento e a outra utiliza a relação de confiança criada para obter vantagem patrimonial.

Como o caso aconteceu em 2022 e os pagamentos retroagem à época dos fatos, o advogado Gabriel Elias explicou que o valor total determinado pela Justiça ultrapassa, atualmente, os R$ 28 mil, considerando-se a correção monetária pela inflação e os honorários advocatícios.

Para Gabriel Elias, a sentença mostrou que o caso não se tratava simplesmente do término precoce de um casamento, mas de uma dinâmica em que a mulher suportava a ampla maioria das despesas, muitas vezes diante de promessas de ressarcimento.

"A sentença deixa um recado muito importante, especialmente aos homens que adotam esse tipo de comportamento: o sentimento de uma mulher não pode ser utilizado como instrumento de exploração patrimonial", afirmou.

Leia a íntegra da nota da defesa do ex-marido:

"Sobre a decisão da 2ª Vara Cível de Anápolis, esclarecemos que se trata de sentença de primeira instância, ainda não transitada em julgado e, portanto, NÃO DEFINITIVA. A defesa vai recorrer: serão interpostos, no prazo legal, os recursos cabíveis para que a decisão seja reexaminada pelo Tribunal de Justiça.

No entendimento da defesa, a sentença comporta reforma, havendo confiança de que será revista na instância superior. Por respeito à intimidade das partes e por se tratar de matéria ainda em discussão judicial (sub judice), ligada à vida privada e familiar, a defesa não comentará o mérito da causa neste momento.

Ficamos à disposição para esclarecimentos de ordem factual.

Laíse de Souza Moreira - OAB/GO 75.614 | Moreira & Cavalcanti Advogados"

articles.title: Observação de aves no Amazonas: 5 locais para ver a fauna nativa | G1
articles.standfirst: De reservas florestais na capital a áreas preservadas no interior do estado, espaços oferecem trilhas, passeios e atividades de observação da fauna amazônica.
articles.summary: A observação de aves no Amazonas ganha destaque em reservas e parques que oferecem trilhas e passeios guiados para contemplar a fauna amazônica em seu habitat.
articles.body:
O estado do Amazonas possui grande diversidade de áreas de floresta abertas para visitação, onde é possível conhecer parte da fauna amazônica em seu habitat natural. Entre unidades de conservação (UCs), reservas particulares e espaços construídos para fins de ecoturismo, atividades como trilhas, passeios ecológicos, caminhadas e atividades específicas de observação de animais ocorrem diariamente, principalmente durante o dia.

Os passeios estão disponíveis tanto em Manaus quanto em municípios do interior do estado. O g1 selecionou cinco locais onde é possível conhecer a fauna amazônica e participar de atividades de ecoturismo disponíveis para os visitantes. Confira abaixo :

Torre de observação do Museu da Amazônia. — Foto: Rubenaldo Ferreira/Musa

O Museu da Amazônia (Musa) ocupa uma área de 100 hectares dentro do Reserva Florestal Adolpho Ducke, do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas da Amazônia (Inpa), em Manaus. Funciona como um museu a céu aberto, reunindo exposições com dados de pesquisas sobre a fauna e flora do local e sete trilhas abertas para passeio diariamente, entre 8h30 e 16h, exceto às quartas-feiras.

Um dos principais atrativos do Musa é a torre de observação de aves, com plataformas a 14, 28 e 42 metros de altura. Lá, visitantes podem levar seus binóculos e equipamentos de fotografia para registrar a fauna e a flora entre 9h às 17h, com visitas especiais para observar o nascer ou o por-do-sol mediante agendamento.

Reserva Particular do Patrimônio Natural Daisaku Ikeda - Manaus

Observação de aves é um dos atrativos dos passeios na RPPN Daisaku Ikeda — Foto: Odette Gonçalves de Araujo/Instituto Soka

A Reserva Particular de Patrimônio Natural (RPPN Daisaku Ikeda) é um espaço de 52 hectares de mata preservada em frente ao Encontro das Águas, onde as águas dos Rio Negro e Rio Solimões se encontram sem se misturar em um trecho de aproximadamente 6km.

O espaço pertence ao Instituto Soka Amazônia, que também promove atividades de turismo no local como caminhadas de observação de aves, passeios ecológicos e trilhas guiadas. Além dos passeios, a reserva também abriga exposições arqueológicas, um viveiro e um mirante com vista para o Encontro das Águas. As visitas devem ser agendadas, e o espaço funciona de segunda a sexta-feira, entre 8h30 e 15h30.

Floresta Nacional de Tefé, no Amazonas — Foto: Jucelino Costa/AmazonasTur

A Floresta Nacional de Tefé é uma Unidade de Conservação (UC) de 865 mil hectares que existe desde 1989, mas passou a fazer parte do catálogo de destinos de turismo de base comunitária apenas nos últimos anos.

Somente na área da floresta, cerca de 1.300 espécies de aves estão catalogadas, além de répteis e mamíferos que podem ser observados e fotografados durante passeios.

Atividades como trilhas interpretativas, caminhadas de observação de aves e visitas a comunidades ribeirinhas são organizadas principalmente pela Associação de Produtores Agroextrativistas da Flona de Tefé e entorno (APAFE), e ocorrem sob agendamento.

Caverna do Maroaga - Presidente Figueiredo

APA Caverna do Maroaga reúne diversas grutas e cachoeiras, onde é possível observar aves, morcegos e peixes. — Foto: Fabricio Ferreira Silva/Arquivo Pessoal

A Área de Proteção Ambiental (APA) Caverna do Maroaga em sua totalidade abriga uma área de 374.700 hectares de um conjunto de cavernas, grutas, cachoeiras e formações geológicas e trechos de floresta. O espaço conta com diversas trilhas que podem ser visitadas com o acompanhamento de guias credenciados todos os dias, entre 8h às 15h30.

Um dos maiores atrativos do local é o complexo de cavernas de formação arenítica onde se localiza a Caverna Refúgio do Maroaga, onde é possível observar diversas espécies de morcegos nativos. Além disso, aves como o Galo-da-serra, simbolo da região, podem ser observadas próximo aos paredões rochosos das cavernas.

A Praia da Velha, no Parna do Jaú, é um dos diversos pontos de observação da fauna na reserva. — Foto: Josângela Jesus/ICMBio

O Parque Nacional do Jaú é uma das maiores Unidades de Conservação de floresta tropical do Brasil, com cerca de 2,2 milhões de hectares em toda a sua área. Lá, são catalogados 445 espécies de aves, mas o número pode ser ainda maior. Também podem ser avistadas diferentes espécies de primatas, répteis e peixes, dependendo da época do ano.

O espaço possui trilhas terrestres e aquáticas, passeios e excursões específicas para observação e fotografia da fauna, tanto durante o dia quanto à noite. A permanência no Parque Nacional do Jaú é permitida 24h por dia, mas a entrada deve ser feita entre 7h e 20h.

Por sua grande extensão, os passeios são organizados por diferentes agências de turismo e podem partir de várias localidades, com acesso por barco ou pelas rodovias AM-070 e AM-352.

Parque Nacional do Jaú, em Novo Airão — Foto: Reprodução/Josângela Jesus

articles.title: Trump quer entregar 40 mil bombas de 1 tonelada a Israel | G1
articles.standfirst: Armamento tem potencial de atingir populações civis, especialmente se usadas em áreas densamente habitadas, como Gaza e cidades do Líbano. Na prática, 'compra' dos artefatos será feita com dinheiro do próprio contribuinte americano.
articles.summary: Armamento tem potencial de atingir populações civis, especialmente se usadas em áreas densamente habitadas, como Gaza e cidades do Líbano.
articles.body:
Ataque aéreo israelense atinge mesquita na Cidade de Gaza, em 28 de julho de 2026 — Foto: Dawoud Abu Alkas/Reuters

O governo Trump pretende realizar maior entrega de bombas da história dos EUA a Israel, num acordo de US$ 2,8 bilhões (R$ 14,4 bilhões) que inclui a transferência de 40 mil artefatos de quase 1 tonelada cada.

A medida, que não foi anunciada oficialmente, vem à tona em um momento de desgaste internacional de Israel, que enfrenta críticas por suas operações militares na Faixa de Gaza e no Líbano, bem como pela violência de colonos israelenses contra palestinos na Cisjordânia, alegadamente com o consentimento de suas forças militares.

Bombas pesadas, como as que fazem parte do acordo, causam preocupação pelo raio de destruição e o potencial de atingir populações civis, especialmente em áreas densamente habitadas, como Gaza .

Segundo os jornais "Washington Post" e "New York Times", entre outros, o governo Trump mandou o texto da proposta reservadamente para duas comissões do Congresso para aprovação informal — ainda que não tenha apoio Legislativo, a Casa Branca dispõe de mecanismos para contornar eventuais vetos para concretizar a entrega.

O acordo prevê a entrega de 20 mil bombas Mark 84 e outras 20 mil bombas BLU-117 . Apesar da nomenclatura, elas são praticamente iguais: pesam aproximadamente uma tonelada curta (equivalente a 907 kg, podendo variar mais ou menos conforme a quantidade de explosivo em seu interior), têm o mesmo formato e são projetadas para ser lançadas de aeronaves.

A diferença está no composto explosivo usado e um revestimento externo para prevenir a explosão acidental em ambientes muito quentes.

Especialistas em armamentos apontam que bombas do tipo podem ser letais em um raio de 300 metros e abrir crateras de até 15 metros de profundidade.

Elas podem ser configuradas para detonar antes, durante ou após o impacto, de acordo com a missão.

Bombas Mark 84/BLU-117 — Foto: Igor Ramon/g1

Embora o acordo seja tratado como uma venda, na prática Israel estaria comprando os armamentos com o dinheiro do próprio contribuinte americano, já que o país recebe US$ 3,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 17 bilhões) por ano dos EUA por meio do programa de Financiamento Militar Estrangeiro (FMF, na sigla em inglês).

Ao menos um congressista se manifestou contra a proposta: o deputado democrata Gregory Meeks, que faz parte da Comissão de Relações Exteriores da casa, disse que não apoiaria o acordo porque ele "levanta preocupações graves e não resolvidas sobre como essas munições poderiam ser utilizadas em áreas densamente povoadas de Gaza e do Líbano".

A condução de Israel em suas campanhas militares em Gaza e no Líbano têm sido alvo de críticas até entre aliados.

Na quarta-feira (16), o ministro da Defesa do pais, Israel Katz, ameaçou retomar a guerra em Gaza e expulsar os palestinos do território , abrindo caminho para o assentamento de colonos israelenses.

O embaixador dos EUA no país, Mike Huckabee, reagiu negando apoiar qualquer plano de "deslocar pessoas para fora de Gaza contra sua vontade".

Os EUA mediaram um cessar-fogo em outubro de 2025 entre Israel e o grupo terrorista Hamas, que pausou a guerra no território palestino e previa um plano de paz e reconstrução.

Na prática, porém, os bombardeios ao território prosseguem.

O ataque terrorista de outubro de 2023 contra Israel, realizado pelo Hamas, matou 1.221 pessoas, segundo uma contagem da agência AFP baseada em números oficiais israelenses. Os combatentes do Hamas também levaram 251 reféns para Gaza.

A campanha de represália de Israel em Gaza matou mais de 73.700 pessoas, segundo o Ministério da Saúde do território, governado pelo Hamas. Além disso, com mais da metade de todas as construções destruídas, boa parte da população está alocada em tendas , sob os efeitos de uma crise humanitária que já dura anos. O número é considerado confiável pela ONU.

A ONU estima que cerca 80% dos prédios em Gaza foram destruídos ou danificados — Foto: REUTERS

Huckabee também criticou, nas últimas semanas, a postura de colonos israelenses na Cisjordânia. O número de episódios violentos envolvendo palestinos tem aumentado nos últimos meses, desde que Israel anunciou planos de abrir novos assentamentos no território, inviabilizando na prática a implantação de um Estado palestino .

No início do mês, Reino Unido e França e mais 10 países anunciam sanções a assentamentos israelenses na Cisjordânia . O governo britânico acusou os colonos de "limpeza étnica".

A Cisjordânia possui alguns bolsões sob controle civil da Autoridade Palestina, mas é controlada militarmente por Israel. Cidadãso palestinos são obrigados a passar por diversos bloqueios e verificações controladas por militares israelenses se quiserem se deslocar pelo território.

Além disso, palestinos da Cisjordânia podem ser detidos sem acusação formal e, se indiciados, podem ser julgados por um tribunal militar de Israel. Colonos israelenses, por sua vez, são julgados por tribunais civis, efetivamente criando um sistema de dois pesos e duas medidas.

O fornecimento de bombas e outros tipos de armamento pelos EUA a Israel ocorre com frequência desde o início da campanha em Gaza, ainda no governo do democrata Joe Biden.

Em meados de 2024, o governo Biden chegou a pausar a entrega das bombas de 1 tonelada a Israel por receio do uso contínuo delas em áreas densamente povoadas. O fornecimento foi destravado por Trump assim que ele retornou à Casa Branca, no início de 2025.

Trump já havia fechado no início de 2026 o fornecimento de outra encomenda de 35 mil bombas Mark 84 e BLU-117 a Israel em fevereiro, por um valor um pouco abaixo do acordado na transação de setembro.

Na prática, é muito difícil o Congresso barrar o envio de armamento a Israel, já que seria necessário um veto de dois terços dos membros nas duas Casas, atualmente de maioria republicana.

Ainda assim, a Casa Branca teria outros meios de contornar um eventual bloqueio. O próprio governo Biden havia declarado emergência no Oriente Médio para não depender do aval do Congresso para concluir a transação nos primeiros meses da guerra em Gaza.

articles.title: Homem em tratamento contra vício em bets fala sobre superação | G1
articles.standfirst: Morador de Salto (SP) conta que começou a apostar por diversão, mas passou a tirar dinheiro de contas da casa e contrair dívidas com agiotas. Psiquiatra explica como as apostas podem afetar o funcionamento do cérebro.
articles.summary: Morador de Salto relata como o vício em bets causou dívidas e perda familiar, enquanto especialista explica os impactos desse transtorno no cérebro.
articles.body:
“Eu já estava no fundo do poço, tinha perdido minha família, perdido o respeito de todos.”

O relato é de um morador de Salto (SP), que não quis se identificar, em tratamento contra a dependência em apostas esportivas, comumente chamadas de bets. O que começou como diversão há cerca de nove anos se transformou em dependência, dívidas e afastamento da esposa e dos filhos.

Após os prejuízos se agravarem, ele decidiu se internar e, desde então, segue em recuperação. Atualmente, ele é paciente de um hospital terapêutico localizado em Capela do Alto (SP).

“Comecei a apostar em bets enquanto trabalhava em uma empresa, há cerca de nove anos. No início, era por diversão. Fui ganhando e perdendo, sempre apostando pouco dinheiro, até o dia em que ganhei uma quantia maior. Foi quando me empolguei”, relata.

Compulsão por jogos de aposta causa graves problemas de saúde mental e provoca afastamentos do trabalho — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

A partir daí, segundo ele, os valores das apostas aumentaram e os primeiros prejuízos começaram a aparecer. Com o avanço do vício, o problema deixou de atingir apenas a vida financeira e passou a afetar também a relação com a família.

“Os problemas familiares começaram, problema em casa com a esposa, perdendo dignidade, perdendo o respeito, porque eu comecei a tirar dinheiro de contas para estar apostando. E cada vez mais o vício foi me corroendo”, diz.

De acordo com o paciente, a situação se agravou quando ele passou a contrair dívidas com agiotas. “Chegou em um ponto que comecei a me envolver com agiotas, comecei a ficar devendo para todo mundo. E assim, cada vez me afundando mais”, relembra.

No fim de 2025, ele conta que já havia perdido a família e o respeito das pessoas próximas. Foi quando decidiu procurar ajuda. A internação durou três meses.

“Foram três meses dolorosos, longe da família, longe dos filhos. E assim, é um processo que machuca a gente. Porque você tem que começar tudo do zero, a ganhar a confiança das pessoas, procurar um novo serviço, e ganhando nome na praça aos poucos e devagar, porque você está com a imagem totalmente queimada. É muito complicado”, relata.

“Apesar de eu estar enfiado no vício, eu sempre fui um pai presente, eu nunca tinha ficado tanto tempo longe dos meus filhos, e a parte mais dolorosa de tudo isso foi afastar as pessoas que eu mais amo por consequência de uns erros meus”, acrescenta.

Depois de enfrentar problemas financeiros, familiares e o período de internação, o paciente afirma que ainda está reconstruindo a vida e recomenda que outras pessoas procurem ajuda antes que a dependência provoque prejuízos maiores.

“E o que eu aconselho para as pessoas que estão perdendo controle sobre as apostas, é para enquanto é tempo. É um dinheiro de ilusão, você não vê a cor dele. Aquela velha história: tudo que vem fácil, vai fácil”, finaliza.

A história do paciente mostra como o comportamento pode deixar de ser recreativo e passar a provocar prejuízos em diferentes áreas da vida. Segundo o psiquiatra Rafael Madureira, de Sorocaba (SP), porém, não é apenas a quantidade de dinheiro ou a frequência das apostas que determina quando o jogo se torna um transtorno.

“Temos uma condição dentro do DSM, que é o Manual Diagnóstico e Estatístico de Transtornos Mentais, que a gente chama de transtorno do jogo. Ele está no capítulo de transtornos relacionados a comportamentos aditivos", explica.

De acordo com Madureira, são considerados nove critérios na avaliação:

Necessidade de apostar valores cada vez maiores para obter a mesma excitação;

Tentativas frustradas de controlar, reduzir ou interromper o jogo;

Irritação ou inquietação ao tentar parar;

Apostar para escapar de problemas ou aliviar sentimentos desagradáveis;

Tentar recuperar perdas financeiras com novas apostas;

Mentir para esconder o envolvimento com o jogo;

Prejudicar relacionamentos, trabalho ou estudos por causa das apostas;

Depender financeiramente de outras pessoas para lidar com dívidas causadas pelo jogo.

Psiquiatra Rafael Madureira de Sorocaba (SP) fala sobre vícios em bets — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Rafael explica que, para o diagnóstico , é necessário apresentar pelo menos quatro desses critérios durante um período de 12 meses, além de sofrimento ou prejuízo significativo.

“A pessoa que aposta ocasionalmente consegue estabelecer limites, consegue interromper a atividade, consegue manter as apostas dentro de uma dimensão recreativa sem que exista esse prejuízo relevante", diz.

Além disso, um dos comportamentos comuns, segundo o psiquiatra, é a tentativa de recuperar o dinheiro perdido por meio de novas apostas.

“A pessoa muitas vezes vai tentar perseguir essa perda, vai tentar recuperar o dinheiro que foi perdido. Então surgem algumas distorções cognitivas. A pessoa acredita que, depois de várias perdas, agora está na vez de ganhar. Pensa: ‘Se eu parar agora, perdi tudo, mas, se eu fizer mais uma jogada, ainda consigo recuperar’", pontua.

Apostas esportivas; bet — Foto: Joédson Alves/Agência Brasil

De acordo com o médico, o transtorno do jogo não está ligado a uma única região do cérebro. O comportamento envolve circuitos relacionados ao sistema de recompensa, à motivação, à aprendizagem, à tomada de decisão e ao controle dos impulsos.

A dopamina também participa desse processo, principalmente na antecipação, na motivação e na aprendizagem relacionadas às recompensas, explica o especialista.

“Não é uma descarga de dopamina. Como esses resultados são imprevisíveis, existe a possibilidade de ganhar, os sinais associados ao jogo e a expectativa do resultado. Tudo isso faz com que a aposta vá se tornando cada vez mais difícil de ignorar", diz.

Rafael também reforça que a dependência não deve ser entendida apenas como uma questão de disciplina individual.

“Aquela questão do ‘jogue com responsabilidade’ coloca como se isso dependesse exclusivamente de uma disciplina individual. Claro que existe uma responsabilidade individual, mas isso não é suficiente para explicar um transtorno aditivo", diz.

“A pessoa pode estar lidando com mecanismos de aprendizagem, impulsividade, sofrimento emocional, a própria publicidade constante e a plataforma desenhada de uma forma para fazer apostar cada vez mais. Então, isso é extremamente delicado", pontua.

O transtorno do jogo também pode aparecer associado a outros problemas de saúde mental, de acordo com Rafael. Estudos apontam que até 82% das pessoas com transtorno do jogo apresentam algum outro transtorno psiquiátrico associado.

Jogo do Tigrinho — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

O psiquiatra explica que cerca de um terço apresenta transtorno relacionado ao uso de substâncias, outro terço tem transtorno de humor e outro, transtorno de ansiedade.

Essa relação, no entanto, pode acontecer nos dois sentidos: uma pessoa que já enfrenta ansiedade, depressão ou um período de estresse pode recorrer às apostas como uma forma de aliviar o sofrimento.

“Não é que o jogo vai necessariamente causar esses transtornos. Às vezes, a via é o contrário. A pessoa que já está em um sofrimento psíquico vai acabar buscando no jogo algum tipo de conforto, algum tipo de solução", acrescenta.

Problemas de sono também são comuns, já que as plataformas podem ser acessadas durante todo o dia, segundo o especialista. Rafael ainda chama a atenção para a relação entre o transtorno do jogo e o risco de suicídio.

“Uma meta-análise recente encontrou uma associação entre o transtorno do jogo e maior risco de ideação suicida, tentativa de suicídio e morte por suicídio.”

De acordo com o psiquiatra, algumas diretrizes internacionais recomendam que profissionais perguntem diretamente sobre pensamentos suicidas a pacientes que apresentam prejuízos importantes relacionados ao jogo.

Saúde Premium, Hospital Terapêutico Integrado localizado em Capela do Alto (SP) — Foto: Divulgação

Segundo Davi Tomasi, diretor financeiro e comercial do Saúde Premium, o hospital terapêutico que tratou o paciente ouvido pela reportagem, houve aumento significativo nas internações relacionadas à dependência em bets, principalmente nos últimos dois anos.

A maior parte dos pacientes tem entre 20 e 40 anos, mas não há um perfil sociocultural específico. “Tem atingido todas as classes sociais, muito provavelmente pelo fácil acesso a esses jogos de apostas", diz.

Ainda conforme o diretor, a maioria dos pacientes procura ajuda quando os prejuízos financeiros e familiares já são significativos. "Quando a gravidade aumenta, as dificuldades em relação ao tratamento aumentam proporcionalmente", explica.

Segundo Davi, o hospital tem observado casos acompanhados de outros transtornos mentais, como ansiedade, depressão e uso de álcool ou outras substâncias.

De acordo com Rafael, o atendimento é individualizado e pode envolver psicólogo, psiquiatra e outros profissionais. Entre as estratégias, o especialista cita a terapia cognitivo-comportamental, que trabalha gatilhos, controle dos impulsos e prevenção de recaídas.

“A entrevista motivacional também pode ajudar a pessoa a reconhecer os prejuízos provocados pelas apostas. A ideia não é ser uma discussão, nenhum sermão, mas conseguir fazer com que a pessoa enxergue quais são os prejuízos associados: o que ela está perdendo em dinheiro, em tempo, em sono, em relações e em tranquilidade”, explica.

Também podem ser adotadas medidas práticas para reduzir o acesso às apostas e evitar recaídas, de acordo com o médico.

“Outra coisa que ajuda muito são as barreiras práticas, como bloquear aplicativos e sites, estabelecer limites financeiros e retirar cartões. Também temos os Jogadores Anônimos, um grupo de ajuda mútua que pode contribuir com uma rede de apoio”, afirma Rafael.

O psiquiatra ainda cita a plataforma centralizada de autoexclusão do Ministério da Fazenda, que permite bloquear o acesso às casas de apostas e impedir novas contas vinculadas ao CPF. Em alguns casos, medicamentos podem ser utilizados para auxiliar no controle de comportamentos impulsivos.

“Não temos nenhum tratamento aprovado especificamente para o transtorno do jogo. O que temos são alguns medicamentos, como a naltrexona e o topiramato, que podem ajudar a controlar o comportamento mais impulsivo”, finaliza.

articles.title: A Suffolk village familiar with tragedy mourns Noah Woods
articles.summary: "This is a community that knows tragedy and has had to contend with tragedy in recent years," says rector.
articles.body:
When three-year-old Noah Woods disappeared, hundreds came together in the hope of bringing him home.

It was at about 15:00 BST on Tuesday when he became separated from a relative while at a playground in Brantham, Suffolk.

The following day the news came that nobody wanted to hear: a child's body had been recovered from a nearby pond.

At least 1,300 people helped to try to find him, coming together in hope then grief. It is not the first time this village of about 2,600 people has been hit by tragedy. Just how does a community come to terms with such a loss?

In July 2024, Anita Rose, 57, who lived in Brantham, was taking her dog Bruce for a morning walk when she was attacked . She died three days later.

It would be three months before her killer Roy Barclay - a violent offender and one of the county's most wanted criminals - was arrested and charged with her murder.

The large police and media presence that descended on Brantham on Tuesday as the search for missing Noah grew, will have brought back painful memories for the village's residents.

Helicopters, dog units and members of the public began scouring the area, close to the River Stour on the Suffolk-Essex border.

Noah was non-verbal and partially deaf, which added complications to the search efforts.

Noah's father Rhys Woods, from nearby East Bergholt, Suffolk, praised those who joined the search.

"The compassion shown by all of you will never be forgotten by us, and brought us comfort and strength at the darkest time of our lives."

Reflecting after Noah's death, the Reverend Chris Willis, rector of St Michael's Church, in Brantham, said: "This is a community that knows tragedy and has had to contend with tragedy in recent years.

"All I can say, unequivocally, is this is a community that has been amazingly positive. It has dealt with the pain of loss and I have no doubt we'll pull together.

"There was a love shown that was my first impression, and I hope and believe we'll see that continue."

James Cartlidge, the MP for South Suffolk, was standing with the volunteers when the police delivered the news of his death.

"That was pretty hard to watch to be honest because they were in deep grief. And that will remain the case," he said.

"I've been many times to Brantham and always get the feeling it is a strong community.

"There's history, there's community, and there is strength. And they showed it with the terrible case with Anita Rose. And they will show it now, and they are showing it now, the way they've responded."

Mal Bridgeman, the chairman of Brantham Parish Council, said he was not sure the community could ever come to terms with the events of the past week.

"I think that Noah will live in the memory of everybody," he said.

"As time goes on, the emotions will quieten down. People will come to terms with it but I think people will just come to terms with it in their own time."

It was a view echoed by the parish council's clerk, Sarah Keys, who said: "People were really hopeful and they felt empowered and really wanted to help.

"So I think finding out that they weren't able to do that anymore was just completely devastating.

"Not the outcome we wanted, but it has really restored your faith in community and in people and in, well, Brantham."

'Be more sensitive and talk to each other'

Canon Yvonne Tulloch founded the charity Ataloss after the death of her husband in 2008. As chief executive, she campaigns for more support for those navigating grief.

She said that as a society, we are not good at acknowledging grief - preferring to convince ourselves that we will live until old age; because of this, emotions can be suppressed and come to the fore following high-profile cases.

"We assume it's next of kin who will be the grievers and, while that is correct, it is not the whole picture.

"There are these ripples, there will be people who will grieve who we wouldn't assume would be doing so.

"Because we've been so poor at understanding grief, what can happen even more is when there is a tragedy that is near to us it makes us think it could have been us - particularly when it involves a child and you're a parent who can relate to it."

Tulloch added this can be "confusing" because those removed from a tragedy can feel they do not have a right to grieve.

She said: "Those who helped with the search have done so because they felt helpless. Equally there will be those who did not help and feel they should have done more.

"In most cases people will have made their decision for sensible reasons and you have to release yourself from guilt and realise you did the best you could."

For the family, there is a balance between appreciating the community support, but not being overwhelmed by it, she said.

"The important thing is not to isolate the family because you do not know what to say.

"People fear saying the wrong thing, but it takes nothing more than acknowledging somebody and saying, 'I'm so sorry, I just want you to know I care'.

"It can mean even more coming from a stranger."

Annie Owen, who volunteers at Ipswich and East Suffolk Samaritans, said that in the modern world, the overload of information can anaesthetise people to many tragedies.

"But for this pure innocent child, there is nowhere to put our reactions or our grief," she said.

Owen said it was important that people do not "beat themselves up" over what they did or did not do.

"So if anybody can find the way of looking at themselves and just thinking, this hurts right now because I'm decent, because I'm caring, because I have a heart. And I think that's a way of easing ourselves through it."

articles.title: I joined Karl Bushby on his round-the-world walk
articles.summary: The BBC heads to Belgium as the adventurer from Hull nears the end of his 28-year expedition.
articles.body:
Adventurer Karl Bushby has been walking around the world for 28 years and now the end of his journey is in sight.

I have been writing about him for most of that time, but although we have spoken frequently and exchanged hundreds of emails we have never met.

We are in the village of Havré and I am joining Karl on a five-mile (8km) stretch to Mons. It is part of the final march to Calais, from where he plans to swim across the English Channel in October.

Dressed in shorts and a T-shirt which bears evidence of a roadside repair, Karl - sporting a grey beard - appears in the car park of a Belgian railway station.

He is pushing a trolley laden with camping equipment and other essentials.

Karl set off from Chile, heading back home to Hull, with two self-imposed rules: he cannot use transport to advance and he cannot return to the UK until the walk is complete.

Sweat is seeping through his T-shirt, forming wing-like patches over his shoulder blades.

The former paratrooper set off in November 1998, expecting his walk back to his childhood home, where his mother still lives, to take about 12 years.

Some 28 years on, he is still going, with visa restrictions, the 2008 financial crash which cost him sponsors, Covid-19 and geopolitics having slowed his progress.

The 57-year-old has covered more than 30,000 miles (more than 48,000km) and a swim across the English Channel now beckons after Channel Tunnel bosses vetoed his request for access to a service tunnel .

Karl ducks into a shop and comes out with a bottle of water, flinging it under a bungee cord attached to his trolley, which he had made in Nicaragua early in the adventure. The Beast, as he calls it, is his lifeline.

We maintain a fast pace. In 30C heat, I am finding it hard to keep up, with Karl showing no sign of fatigue, despite having trekked 10 miles before lunch.

We talk about how he crossed the frozen Bering Strait in 2006 with French adventurer Dimitri Kieffer and his 186-mile swim across the Caspian Sea .

Discussing his crossing of the Darién Gap, which links Colombia and Panama, Karl says: "You're having to push through a dense jungle.

"You've got these river systems and lots of swamps. Laid over the top of that you've got the fact that it's a warzone."

Faced with the threat of kidnap, Karl sought to look as though he was homeless.

"Homeless people are pretty much invisible, nobody pays attention to them, so that was our intent.

"I did not want to be the blond-haired, blue-eyed gringo with the latest North Face equipment.

"I dyed my hair and skin and reduced my clothing to tatters. I carried my stuff in sacks."

A woman peers out of a window and looks bemused at the sight of two men and a trolley.

Karl invites me to push The Beast for a short while. The black fabric tape covering the handle is worn and peeling.

With each passing mile, our conversation becomes more philosophical.

I ask him what the biggest lessons have been on the walk.

Karl struggles to weave The Beast past a row of parked cars. "These towns can be fun assault courses," he sighs.

Returning to the question, he adds: "Coming from a military background, you don't necessarily see the best in people, so it has really been an eye-opener.

"From day one, I have been received with open arms from the rest of the world."

Karl talks about the "kindness of strangers", noting how one family in Chile became "almost like a second family".

"They were driving out for eight hours at a time to find me and feed me on the side of the road," he recalls.

I reach into my rucksack and retrieve a letter from Karl's mother, Angela Bushby. Also in the bag are packets of his favourite sweets.

"Mother remembers," he laughs, selecting the caramel wafers.

"You're still her little boy, aren't you?" I ask.

"Apparently so," says Karl. "A very happy little boy with all that chocolate."

In the letter, Angela asks if he really must swim the Channel. Both mother and son know the answer.

And then comes a line that speaks volumes.

"You used to think you were useless. Well, you have proven you're not," Angela has written.

I have always known Karl to be self-deprecating, but this leaps from the page.

He tells me he never felt as fit as his fellow comrades during his Army days.

Karl, whose father served in the SAS, says the Army helped build his confidence, but the "damage was done" in his early childhood, with undiagnosed dyslexia making him a target for bullies.

"I had no confidence," he says. "I was an underachiever. My dyslexia was not identified until my last year in school."

Karl, though, has never doubted he could finish his journey.

"There is definitely this sense of wanting to prove myself," he says. "To myself and others. We're talking about doing something other people couldn't even dream of doing."

For years, Karl has been relaxed about the end date. Not now. There is a real urgency.

"It's definitely time to call it a day," he says. "I don't want to keep this going for much longer."

We reach Mons and the impressive Grand-Place, where several young people, recognising him from his Instagram account, make a beeline for him.

"Oh my God, you are a legend," one excited young man tells Karl.

"Yes," he admits. "One day I'm going to wake up in my mother's house – 57 years old with nothing but my stuff in a bag next to the bed."

We arrive at a cafe and Karl orders an orange juice.

I ask him what the hardest part of the journey has been, but instead of talking about blisters or fears about crime, he says: "It's the relationships. I've fallen in love twice, lost them, and that leaves marks.

"The physical pain stuff – yeah, that's all doable. In terms of falling in love and then having to just carry on the walk? You're going to lose it."

He tells me he gets a "real buzz from a good horizon".

It will surely not get much better than the first sight of the white cliffs of Dover.

As we stand in a beautiful square, the famous Belfry of Mons looming over us, I ask Karl if he ever pauses to truly soak up the sights.

"Sometimes you just don't have the energy," he admits.

"In a place like this, you'll take it in. You'd be surprised how many times I found myself in a place reminding myself I will never be here again."

I hope our paths will cross again... on English soil.

articles.title: Ceredigion councillor faces 'hatred' online after sharing RNLI video
articles.summary: Elizabeth Evans, who shared a video of an RNLI training exercise, says the comments were "really, really bad".
articles.body:
A woman who shared an RNLI video on social media says she has received "pure hatred" following anti-migrant protests in England.

Councillor Elizabeth Evans, who represents Aberaeron and Aberarth in Ceredigion, shared a video on Facebook which showed New Quay's RNLI lifeboat leaving the station on a training day.

According to Evans, the post - which attracted 30,000 views - drew comments of hatred, some of which she described as "really, really bad".

It comes after RNLI volunteers in Portsmouth were targeted by protesters following the charity's role in helping to bring migrants on a small boat to shore earlier this month.

The RNLI said it existed "to save lives at sea".

Evans said she was "really shocked" by the reaction to the video.

"And it wasn't a few. It took me a good half hour to get rid of those comments, just one after the other. With that thread of hatred."

Describing the comments, Evans continued: "The comment thread was 'traitors', 'taxis for migrants', they were some of the politest ones."

She said one of the comments was suggestive of violence, adding: "I don't want to go on because I don't want to give those comments oxygen but they were really, really bad."

Evans said she deleted the comments but was subsequently criticised for "shutting down discussion".

"I wasn't shutting down discussion because there was no discussion available to be had," she said. "I was shutting down hatred."

Peter Sparkes, chief executive of the RNLI, said recent events had "generated deliberate misinformation and a misunderstanding about the RNLI".

"Our mission, and our tasking is to rescue those women, children and men in danger of drowning.

"Anyone rescued from a small boat by the RNLI is immediately handed over to the UK's immigration authorities.

"Illegal immigration is a political issue; the RNLI exists to save lives at sea."

Small boat protest explained: How a Channel crossing sparked unrest

Track UK's latest migration numbers - net migration, visas, asylum and small boats

A total of 16,513 people arrived in the UK in small boats in the year to 1 September, 43% lower than the same period the previous year.

UK net migration has meanwhile dropped to its lowest level outside of the Covid pandemic since 2012.

Evans said social media platforms should do more to crackdown on online abuse and urged the UK government to help.

"They need to enforce through legislation that these companies have an absolute responsibility to make sure that they keep their users safe but also, that it's not used as a platform for hatred… We must not allow it to be normalised," said Evans.

The UK government said those who dedicated themselves to the service of others should be able to do their work without fear of harassment or abuse online, adding that Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy expected social media companies to be more proactive and rigorous in removing harmful content.

A spokesperson for Meta, which owns several social media platforms including Facebook, said "no one should be subjected to abuse of any kind" adding that it removes harmful content when it finds it.

articles.title: Why are London's flats becoming harder to sell?
articles.summary: James Schaife and his partner are among the many Londoners struggling to sell their flat.
articles.body:
In 2015, thousands of people queued overnight in the rain to reserve and buy studio apartments selling for under £200,000 in Hounslow, west London.

It's in stark contrast to today's appetite for flats, with property portals reporting a slump in sales.

But why, when the country is in a housing crisis with a desperate need for affordable homes , are flats now struggling to sell?

According to the property site Zoopla, 88% of flats listed for sale in inner London on its website in 2025 did not find a buyer within six months. The company also says the gap between the value of a flat and a house is the widest it has been for 30 years.

Executive director Richard Donnell points to post-pandemic social changes with "people looking for space, prioritising houses, working from home".

He also points to higher mortgage rates, people concerned about "all the costs and liabilities of owning a property" including service charges and ground rents.

In September, nearly all the major mortgage lenders in the UK announced increases in the cost of home loans.

Donnell says flats in inner London are struggling in particular as they are more expensive, the service charges are higher, and "there's greater complexity - it's highly likely it's a bigger building, maybe more of a complex building, so less are selling within six months".

This is a message echoed by property platform Rightmove, which says as of August, only 50% of flats listed for sale nationally successfully find a buyer, compared to 65% of houses.

Nationally, as of August, the average price for a flat is down 2% from 12 months prior. That is the largest drop seen over the period by any type of property.

Compared with August 2021, flats have only risen in price by 4% nationally, the least of all property types.

Colleen Babcock, Rightmove's head of partner marketing, says London faces additional challenges because its market is heavily weighted towards flats, and "affordability more broadly remains a key challenge".

She points to higher borrowing costs, increased stamp duty costs , and the limitations of the Lifetime ISA in higher-priced areas, which mean both first-time buyers and home-movers in London can face additional hurdles when buying a home.

Flats aren't becoming unsellable for one single reason. Higher borrowing costs, service charges, leasehold and shared ownership complications have made them more expensive and complicated to own, damaging their reputation.

James Schaife, 36, says he and his partner are "on the verge of bankruptcy" after struggling to sell their one-bedroom north London flat for the past four years.

He bought a 35% share of the £585,000 flat - run by Newlon Housing Trust - in 2017, but after his partner got a new job, James moved out of London in 2022 and relocated north, putting the flat on the market.

Within an initial "nomination period" - a set window of time where the association has the exclusive right to find an eligible buyer - the flat generated next to no interest.

The housing association gave them permission to sell it on the open market - but James claims they have been "forced to use a narrow selection of valuers chosen by Newlon", despite estate agents telling him the flat has been overvalued.

They have been forced to rent out the property with a special "consent-to-let" agreement with their housing association - although this is due to expire imminently and James claims Newlon will not renew it.

James said the situation has affected their plans to start a family, pushing them back to an age "where it's probably unlikely that we'll have children".

A spokesperson for Newlon Housing Trust said that "this is not a picture we recognise", adding that they were bound by "strict rules about resales to protect the public purse".

The spokesperson said that "strict rules to limit subletting... prevent the risk of people profiting by letting subsidised affordable housing".

"As is well reported, the sales market is flat. The saleability of a home at any time is subject to variation in the property market, which we have no control over, and is part of the risk taken on by anyone who buys a home."

Some flat-owners living in homes with building safety concerns have also found their properties impossible to sell.

It may be a more extreme example, but many find themselves in this position.

As of July 2026, there are 4,697 residential buildings 11m and over in height being monitored due to unsafe cladding , but work still isn't complete on 61% of them.

Sophie Bichener, leaseholder and campaigner with the End our Cladding Scandal group, said that flats with unsafe cladding left unremediated were like "prisons", and this is having a "devastating" impact on people's lives.

She bought her one-bedroom flat in Hertfordshire in 2017 but nine years later, now with a young family, she is unable to move to a bigger property as her building needs a second wave of fire safety repairs.

"Being trapped means that you can't move on with your life."

She points out that even buildings which have been remediated are affected by a market that is "so distrusting" at the moment.

"If you're in a position where you can get to market, there are so many hurdles... management packs costing hundreds of pounds, conveyancing solicitors not willing to take on buildings covered by the Building Safety Act."

Sophie thinks there should be a building safety register, "where you've got all the buildings noted, and we know what they're made of" to help boost buyer confidence.

The BBC has also investigated problems with new-build properties , including people living in brand-new flats.

Their stories come as the number of complaints to the New Homes Ombudsman Service has more than tripled in a year, according to its latest annual report.

The UK-wide service received just over 1,800 complaints in 2025-26, up from fewer than 600 the previous year. Defects and snagging were the most common issues raised.

The ombudsman says the increase partly reflects more homeowners being eligible to use the service, as well as greater awareness of it.

At the same time, developers say building new homes is becoming more expensive, adding to pressure on London's already limited housing supply.

Home-builders estimate that the cost of delivering a new property has risen by an estimated average of £76,000 per home, equivalent to more than 20% of the average new home value of £365,000.

They claim the increase is down to higher labour and material costs, additional regulations, and tax and levy rises.

James Stevens, director for cities at the Home Builders Federation (HBF), said: "The collapse of London's housing supply presents a real threat to the capital's economic and social prospects.

"Housing starts in London have fallen to an alarmingly low level and have been on a downward trend for some time. An urgent overhaul of housing and planning policy is now critical to supporting the housing needs of all Londoners – particularly the capital's first-time buyers who face the biggest barriers to home ownership in the country."

The HBF also reported in October 2024 that there were 17,432 Section 106 affordable units that remain unallocated.

Zoopla's executive director Richard Donnell says affordability needs to improve.

"I think everyone's hoping that mortgage rates come down. The government's announced some reforms to leasehold to improve some of the certainty. They focused on the transparency and so buyers can get more of an understanding of what they're buying."

He says there could be a reduction in marriage value, which is a payment to extend the lease on a flat with fewer than 80 years remaining, and make it "much clearer and easier for tenants and long leaseholders to take more control of their costs and destiny".

Charged £720 to have a key cut - soaring bills drive leaseholders to breaking point

'It's ruined my life': Flat-owner says building work by freeholder has left her homeless

A spokesperson for the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said "We're taking decisive action to help people up and down the country to buy and sell flats with greater confidence, including in London.

"Our Mortgage Guarantee Scheme will support homebuyers with a deposit as small as 5%, while we're also capping ground rents at £250 and ending the use of leasehold entirely for new homes , which will make it more attractive to buy flats.

"This is alongside speeding up cladding removal to bring the building safety crisis to an end and forcing those responsible to fix unsafe buildings or face criminal prosecution."

A spokesperson for the Mayor of London Lord Khan said: "City Hall is working with London boroughs, housing associations, developers and others to deliver more homes of all tenures that Londoners so desperately need.

"The mayor has consistently stood up for Londoners by advocating for an end to the outdated feudal leasehold system once and for all, and we welcome steps from government to make commonhold the default tenure and ban the sale of leasehold flats.

"To protect leaseholders, the mayor has already launched the Service Charges Charter to bring much-needed transparency and fairness to how service charges are handled.

"Alongside this, City Hall actively funds our housing partners to acquire homes from the private sector and convert them into secure social and affordable housing, providing housing for those most in need and putting housing stock to good use."

We often hear that London desperately needs more affordable housing, but a combination of higher mortgage rates, changing preferences, leasehold costs and building safety problems - which influences the reputation of flats - is making one of the capital's most common types of home harder to sell.

So perhaps the problem isn't simply a shortage of homes, but rather - are we building and selling the wrong homes?

articles.title: In 2024, Narelle Zanker turned her 4,000-acre family dairy farm into a classroom; 2 years later, her Dairy Adventures had welcomed 1,200+ visitors and won the 2026 Rural Women’s Award
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In 2024, Narelle Zanker turned her 4,000-acre family dairy farm near Mannum into a living classroom where visitors could bottle-feed calves, watch mil.
articles.body: In 2024, Narelle Zanker turned her 4,000-acre family dairy farm near Mannum into a living classroom where visitors could bottle-feed calves, watch milking in action and learn where their food really comes from. Two years later, her agritourism venture Dairy Adventures had welcomed more than 1,200 guests and earned her the 2026 AgriFutures Rural Women’s Award for South Australia, followed by the national title at Parliament House in Canberra. According to AgriFutures Australia, the former teacher was recognised for bridging the gap between farmers and consumers through hands-on education and regional tourism, with new plans to reach even more students through virtual farm lessons and school resources.From classroom to cowshedNarelle Zanker grew up on her family’s mixed farming property near Mannum, about an hour east of Adelaide on the Murray River. After spending four years working as a school teacher, she returned to the farm with a clear idea. She wanted to combine her love of education with her lifelong connection to dairying. With support from her husband Joel and wider family, she launched Dairy Adventures in 2024 as the only agritourism experience of its kind in South Australia.The venture operates on a working 4,000-acre dairy and mixed farm that milks around 300 cows with year-round calving. Instead of a static display farm, visitors step into a real food production facility. They tour the dairy, watch mechanised milking in action, learn about calf rearing and biosecurity, and hear how milk moves from paddock to plate. Zanker has woven teaching frameworks into every tour so that preschoolers, school groups, families, aged-care residents and disability groups all leave with a clearer picture of modern farming.A farm that teachesDairy Adventures runs up to four tours a week and offers experiences that feel more like play than a lecture. Guests bottle-feed calves, try their hand at milking, meet the herd and even visit favourites like Elvis the steer. For many city families and grandparents, these moments reconnect them with rural life they remember from their own childhoods. For students, the visit becomes a living science lesson about animal care, food safety and the systems behind everyday groceries.In its first year alone, the business welcomed more than 1,200 visitors and earned a silver medal in the New Tourism Business category at the 2025 South Australian Tourism Awards. That rapid growth showed there was strong demand for transparent, paddock-to-plate experiences that let people ask questions and see the work behind their food.Recognition and next stepsZanker’s work caught the attention of AgriFutures Australia, which runs the Rural Women’s Award to celebrate innovation and leadership by women in regional industries. In May 2026 she was named the South Australian winner, receiving a $15,000 Westpac grant to improve accessibility on the farm, develop interactive features and create educational resources with Dairy Australia. She also planned a children’s book about life on a dairy farm for schools and libraries.Later that year, she took the next step by winning the national AgriFutures Rural Women’s Award at a gala dinner at Parliament House in Canberra. As national winner she received an additional $20,000 grant to expand Dairy Adventures further, including building a virtual classroom program so students across Australia can join live lessons from the farm even if they cannot visit in person.Why the story mattersAt a time when fewer Australians live on farms, initiatives like Dairy Adventures help rebuild trust and understanding between producers and consumers. Zanker has said the goal is not just to show a pretty farm, but to help people see the science, systems and care in every bottle of milk. By turning a working dairy into a classroom, she is creating a new model for agricultural education that is both commercially viable and deeply community focused.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Richard Tice accuses Sarah Cooper-Lesadd of 'lying about her beliefs' before switching from Reform UK to Plaid Cymru
articles.summary: Sarah Cooper-Lesadd, who left Reform this week, also revealed she had voted Remain in the 2016 EU referendum.
articles.body:
Reform UK's deputy leader has accused the party's former Senedd Member Sarah Cooper-Lesadd of lying to them about her political beliefs before she defected to Plaid Cymru.

Richard Tice was speaking after a chaotic week for his party in which its Welsh leader resigned after being arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour.

Helen Jenner, the party's deputy leader in Wales, is favourite to take over next week.

Tice insisted the events had not distracted the party from the issues it was tackling, saying there were good days and bad days in politics.

Plaid Cymru said Cooper-Lesadd had been "honest about her political beliefs" and had acknowledged her views had changed.

Sarah Cooper-Lesadd, who was elected to the Pen-y-bont Bro Morgannwg constituency, made the dramatic political move to Plaid Cymru , claiming Reform UK was "far more interested in division, opposition and headlines than in finding solutions".

As well as saying she was now a supporter of Welsh independence, she also revealed she had voted to Remain in the EU referendum a decade ago.

When asked how she had got through the vetting process as a Remain voter, Tice said: "If someone deliberately misleads you, and fibs to you, and lies to you, then it doesn't matter how much vetting you do.

"So, why don't you ask her that question? How can you turn from being a unionist to a separatist?

"How can you turn from being someone who believes in defending our borders to want to open the borders and become a nation of sanctuary? The whole thing's absurd," he told BBC Radio Wales Sunday Supplement.

"I'm not in charge of vetting. Look, we make lots of brilliant, fast-moving decisions and judgements.

"That's why we've grown to be the second-largest party in Wales so quickly from a standing start. We never claim that we're perfect. You know, we're real people."

Tice refused to confirm whether Helen Jenner would take over from Thomas next week other than to say that whoever becomes leader will get the seal of approval from him and the UK leader Nigel Farage.

Thomas, who was released on bail after his arrest, stood down saying he had done nothing wrong but did not want to be a distraction to the party.

He has not been suspended from the party - which would have effectively left him as an independent MS - while Gwent Police continues its investigation.

Senedd member Sarah Cooper-Lesadd quits Reform to join Plaid Cymru

Helen Jenner likely to take over as Reform Wales leader, sources tell BBC

Tice said the events had not distracted Reform Senedd Members from focusing on issues such as the housing of illegal migrants, small boats crossing the English Channel and the 20mph speed limit.

He said: "Life is work in progress. But the bottom line is that we've got a group of 33 elected representatives, and they're the second largest party by a considerable margin, and we're raising issues that are absolutely vital to the residents of Wales.

"Life moves at different paces, and you have sometimes good days, you have sometimes bad days.

"The reality is that very shortly, we'll have a new leader. But our representatives are getting on with the job of representing their constituents and raising issues they want raised."

A Plaid Cymru spokesperson said: "Sarah has been honest about her political journey and has acknowledged that her views have changed since she first entered politics."

You can see more of the interview on Politics Wales on BBC One Wales at 10:00 on Sunday and on BBC iPlayer.

articles.title: In 2025, Florida salvagers found more than 1,000 gold and silver coins from a 1715 wreck off the Treasure Coast; the salvage company estimated the haul at $1 million
articles.summary: US News: In 2025, divers recovered over 1,000 gold and silver coins estimated at $1 million from a 1715 shipwreck off Florida's Treasure Coast, shedding light on a historic maritime disaster and treasure hunting legacy.
articles.body: For more than three centuries, the Atlantic waters off Florida have held reminders of a Spanish fleet that met disaster on its journey home. In 2025, divers returned to that underwater landscape and recovered a remarkable cache of more than 1,000 gold and silver coins. The discovery, made during the summer salvage season, was estimated by the salvage company at about $1 million, adding another chapter to one of Florida's most famous shipwreck stories.According to the Associated Press, the artefacts include 1,051 silver reales, five gold escudos, and other gold objects recovered along Florida’s Atlantic coast. The coins have been identified as having been struck in the Spanish colonies of Mexico, Bolivia, and Peru. Many of the coins still bear dates and mint marks. Captain Levin Shavers and his crew aboard the M/V Just Right carried out the recovery for 1715 Fleet – Queen’s Jewels LLC. They are responsible for the exclusive salvage of the wrecks.The hurricane that changed Florida's coastThe coins had lain on the seabed for nearly 310 years since the hurricane struck the Spanish treasure ships, which were travelling from Havana to Spain on July 31, 1715. The ships carried gold and other valuables the Spanish had collected from their colonies in the Americas. According to NOAA, about 2,500 sailors and passengers were aboard the fleet, and around 1,000 died when the hurricane struck. The disaster scattered wreckage and treasure along Florida’s east coast, with the surviving material eventually contributing to the area’s association with treasure hunting and the name “Treasure Coast”.The hunt for that lost treasure is nothing new. Salvage activities have been taking place for decades, with treasure hunters recovering coins and other items from these shipwrecks. Kip Wagner is among those who made their mark as an early salvor, with thousands of silver coins being retrieved by his crew in the 1960s.A cache hidden beneath the sandThe discovery made in 2025 seems to have been very localised in its nature. Many of the coins were found in one place, and the salvagers think they may originally have been stored in a bag or bundle that broke apart when the ship sank. Some of the coins reportedly had marks suggesting they had been inside a burlap bag. The dates found on the coins also give us some idea of the money that may have been carried aboard the ship shortly before its sinking. Reports about the discovery say some of the coins date from the late 17th century to 1714, reflecting the range of currency that could have been in circulation when the 1715 fleet set sail.According to the National Park Service, shipwreck sites can provide valuable archaeological evidence about maritime trade and past societies, making the location and relationship of artefacts important beyond their monetary value. A coin recovered from its original archaeological setting can provide information about its date, mint and movement, while its position alongside other objects can help researchers reconstruct patterns of trade and exchange across the Spanish Empire. It is especially significant in Florida, where the practice of treasure recovery is long intertwined with archaeology. Underwater cultural resources in Florida are regulated, and removing historic artefacts from state-owned waters without proper authorisation is illegal. The 1715 Fleet–Queens Jewels project carries out its operations through authorised salvage agreements.What happens to the recovered coins?However, the salvaged fragments do not just end up being taken out of the ocean and exhibited. The artefacts get catalogued first, and information like the age, mint markings, weight and recovery location of each coin is recorded. Afterwards, the coins undergo conservation, which includes cleaning aimed at removing the salt deposits while preserving the metal structure.Under Florida's system, the state may keep some of the recovered archaeology for study and exhibition. The rest is split up in accordance with the salvage contracts and judicial supervision involved. This suggests that more artefacts may still be buried under the sand. More than 300 years after the fleet sank, changing sea floors, weather, and shifting sands continue to uncover artefacts that were hidden for centuries. For treasure hunters, the discovery is a major find. But for historians and archaeologists, the importance of the find is that the 1,000-plus coins might be able to tell them much about the people who went on the journey in 1715.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2024, New York released dye into Patchogue Bay to track treated wastewater and help protect shellfish waters, beaches and bay wildlife downstream
articles.summary: US News: In March 2024, New York conducted a dye study in Patchogue Bay to track treated wastewater and assess its impact on local shellfish and water quality, utilizing Rhodamine WT dye as a tracer for effective environmental management.
articles.body: For a few hours in March 2024, parts of the Patchogue River and Patchogue Bay on Long Island could take on an unusual red or pink appearance. The colour was not caused by pollution or an algal bloom. Scientists had deliberately added a fluorescent dye to treated wastewater, creating a visible tracer that could reveal where the water travelled after leaving a treatment plant.This experiment aimed to answer a practical question: what happens to treated wastewater that enters the Patchogue River and Bay? This question matters because the surrounding waters are used for shellfish production, and water movement affects how quickly pollutants would spread in the event of a spill or dumping.Why the wastewater needed a closer lookAccording to the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC), the hydrographic dye study was conducted jointly with the US Food and Drug Administration between March 24 and 30, 2024. Low concentrations of Rhodamine WT, a water-tracing dye approved by the US Environmental Protection Agency, were introduced into wastewater at the Village of Patchogue Wastewater Treatment Plant on March 25 for about 12.4 hours. The dye was expected to make sections of the Patchogue River and Patchogue Bay appear red or pink temporarily. The purpose was not to test whether the wastewater itself was safe. Instead, researchers wanted to understand its flow and dispersion after discharge. That information could help DEC and the FDA determine the appropriate shellfish closure area around the treatment plant's outfall.This was especially important because shellfish can accumulate contaminants from the water. Knowing how fast the effluent moved and how far it travelled gave officials useful information for deciding where shellfish harvesting should be prohibited. The study was also used for contingency planning in case something happened at the treatment plant and there was a spill.Research published in Estuaries and Coasts suggests that water movement in the Long Island South Shore Estuary is strongly affected by tidal exchange, channel shape and circulation. A study of the Patchogue, Swan and Carmans rivers found that the Patchogue River experienced significant water-quality problems, including periods of low dissolved oxygen, while restricted water exchange could contribute to poor flushing.Following the dye through the bayThe experiment was based on a simple idea: once researchers know when and where the dye is injected, they can trace its path. Using equipment and monitoring stations, they measured the levels of the dye as it flowed from the river to the bay. The selection of Rhodamine WT dye was significant because it can be detected at very low concentrations. The DEC assured people that the amount to be used would not pose any threat to the environment.The study also built upon earlier research showing that Patchogue Bay is influenced by several different potential sources of contamination. A US Geological Survey investigation examined groundwater, stormwater, ponds, wetlands, marinas and the wastewater treatment plant as possible contributors to faecal contamination. It found that stormwater and drainage from ponds and wetlands were the most substantial transport mechanisms identified in Patchogue Bay, while the treatment plant was not considered a likely major source of faecal contamination based on the study's microbial-marker results. That distinction is important. Tracking treated wastewater does not mean that all contamination found in the bay originates from the treatment plant. Instead, the dye study was intended to establish how this particular discharge moves through the water system, providing information that can be considered alongside other identified contamination pathways when assessing conditions in the bay.What the experiment could revealThe information gathered may help define the boundaries of the wastewater discharge area where shellfish harvesting is prohibited. It could also serve as a reference point for future incidents. Additionally, a study in Estuaries and Coasts found that circulation and flushing in the larger Great South Bay can vary greatly depending on tides, wind and inlet configuration. These factors influence the time that water stays in different areas of the estuary. That is why Patchogue used a real tracer: computer models can estimate circulation, but the dye provides a field-based comparison. As a result, the experiment became a way to track wastewater movement through the bay. For scientists, the temporary colour change was a way to trace the water’s path and gather data for managing shellfish waters.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
